ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

rockwood — pattern 1

A rugby player lands on the lateral shoulder. There is focal AC joint tenderness, but radiographs show no displacement or increased coracoclavicular distance. Assessment indicates a mild AC ligament sprain with the coracoclavicular ligament complex remaining intact. Which Rockwood acromioclavicular injury type best fits this pattern?

  1. Type III
  2. Type IV
  3. Type V
  4. Type I
  5. Type II
Answer and explanation

Type I

Type I: An AC ligament sprain with intact coracoclavicular ligaments and no radiographic displacement.

Option explanations

Type I: Type I: An AC ligament sprain with intact coracoclavicular ligaments and no radiographic displacement.

Type II: Type II describes aC ligament disruption with coracoclavicular ligament sprain and mild displacement. The case instead matches Type I.

Type III: Type III describes complete AC and CC ligament disruption with superior displacement and a coracoclavicular distance increase of about 25–100%. The case instead matches Type I.

Type IV: Type IV describes posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into or through the trapezius. The case instead matches Type I.

Type V: Type V describes marked superior displacement with extensive deltotrapezial disruption and a coracoclavicular distance increase greater than 100%. The case instead matches Type I.
